subject.title: feat: AI safety event taxonomy — plugin emission API and manifest policy

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this six-event AI-safety taxonomy and a permanent manifest-gated emission contract for external plugins?
rationale: The change creates long-lived plugin SDK, manifest, telemetry, trust, and compatibility contracts whose taxonomy and policy cannot be selected safely by automated patch review.

options.title: Sponsor a host-bound contract
options.body: Approve the direction, but require the API to be rebuilt around host-created identity, manifest, session, and runtime-validation authority before merge.

options.title: Keep taxonomy core-only
options.body: Allow trusted core diagnostics to emit the events but omit external plugin permissions and the public plugin emission surface.

options.title: Decline the taxonomy series
options.body: Keep existing generic diagnostics and external telemetry integrations rather than adding a permanent first-class safety taxonomy.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a host-bound contract
recommendation.body: Approve the direction, but require the API to be rebuilt around host-created identity, manifest, session, and runtime-validation authority before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent plugin API and manifest work makes them the strongest available routing candidate for the permanent contract decision.
